lock_rationale: Written ONCE, before any v1.1 hypothesis was tested, and read-only for the whole v1.1 research phase. It is a separate FILE from gate_policy.json because v1.0's bytes are hashed into every entry of the published record (`policy_sha256`); editing that file would leave the record unable to name the policy it ran under. NO THRESHOLD IN THIS FILE DIFFERS FROM v1.0. The diff between the two files is exactly: the version string, the lock time and rationale, the `target_universe` declaration, an added `v1_1_changes` disclosure block, and the three family names in `families_enabled`. Every other value is copied unchanged, so a reader can verify the claim 'nothing was loosened' by diffing two files instead of trusting this sentence.
target_universe_rationale: DISCLOSED SPECIFICATION CHOICE. BTCUSDT is the target not because the data suggested it but because of the VENUE: it is the only instrument this project has verified its Agent Hub execution path can actually place an order on (accepted demo orders 1485970832289546240 and the one before it). Every rToken is refused by the demo venue before any sizing or balance check (`papTradingService not support RWA order validation error`), so v1.0's promoted factor had no reachable venue no matter what its statistics said. Choosing a target by execution reachability is a specification choice made with knowledge of the venue, and it is stated here rather than presented as a data-driven finding. It does not bias the statistics: the backtest still measures the same thing on the same frozen data, and the same thresholds apply. ETHUSDT is deliberately EXCLUDED even though this system reads its candles — its venue reachability has never been verified, and assuming it would repeat the exact mistake this list exists to prevent.

v1_1_changes.target_universe: rToken list (default, undeclared) -> ["BTCUSDT"]. The v1.0 list is untouched in types.ts and remains what a policy gets when it declares nothing.
v1_1_changes.families_enabled: funding_to_rtoken / btc_momentum_to_rtoken / combined_cross_asset -> funding_to_pair / momentum_to_pair / combined_to_pair. NEW NAMES, not widened meanings: a durable record entry reading `funding_to_rtoken` must keep meaning a funding signal tested against a tokenised equity. The v1.0 names and their FAMILY_SIGNALS entries remain in the code and remain valid.
v1_1_changes.thresholds: UNCHANGED. fdr_level 0.10, min_ic 0.04, min_t_stat 2.0, min_obs 100, require_baseline_beat true, sampling non_overlapping — all identical to v1.0.
v1_1_changes.sampling: UNCHANGED — non_overlapping, for the same reason as v1.0: overlapping forward windows share return data and inflate t-statistics.
v1_1_changes.kill_reason_precedence: UNCHANGED — the same five checks in the same order.
v1_1_changes.execution_guard: UNCHANGED — the same five checks and the same caps.
v1_1_changes.what_this_phase_does_NOT_change: The production loop still runs v1.0. The LLM prompt, the hypothesis schema validator and the session loop continue to offer and accept the rToken universe, because switching the RUNNING system to a new policy version is a separate change with its own blast radius. v1.1 is a research phase, and it says so.

sampling_rationale: Observations are sampled at intervals of at least the forward-window length (one 4h obs per 4h block), so no two observations share return data. Testing every minute would produce ~606 overlapping 4h-forward observations per weekday that share 239/240 of their data, inflating t-statistics by roughly sqrt(240) ~ 15x and promoting noise. Non-overlapping sampling costs observation count but keeps every observation independent and keeps the significance claim honest. This is preregistered and must be disclosed.

power_analysis.note: Inherited UNCHANGED from v1.0, where it was pre-registered BEFORE any hypothesis was tested. It was measured on rToken candles (RCOINUSDT), NOT on BTCUSDT, so it is a statement about the rToken universe and is carried here only to document why the forward-window cap is 120 minutes. The v1.1 measurement on BTCUSDT is recorded separately in the phase's metadata artifact rather than substituted into this block after the fact.
power_analysis.cap_rationale: At 480 minutes only 70 valid observations exist, below min_obs=100, so an 8-hour hypothesis would auto-KILL for insufficient data rather than on the merits of the idea. Capping at 120 minutes keeps every reachable hypothesis testable. The 15-30 minute range carries the statistical power; windows beyond 2 hours require an IC above 0.1, which real markets essentially never produce.
power_analysis.ic_floor_note: min_ic = 0.04 only binds once n >= ~2500, which occurs only at the 15-minute window. At every longer window the t-statistic floor is the binding constraint. The IC floor is retained as a sanity check, not as the operative bar.
power_analysis.v1_1_expectation_noted_before_the_run: BTCUSDT trades continuously, including weekends, whereas rTokens collapse to 2-8% coverage on weekends. Observation counts for a BTCUSDT target are therefore expected to be HIGHER than the rToken figures above, which may make the IC floor bind at the 15-minute window for the first time. That is recorded here as an expectation formed before the run, and the measured counts go in the metadata artifact.

multiple_testing_note: The Benjamini-Hochberg correction counts EVERY hypothesis attempted this session, including all kills, retries, schema rejections, and near-duplicates. The count must never be limited to hypotheses that passed. In v1.1 the family is the COMPLETE preregistered enumeration (320 hypotheses), known before the first backtest ran, so m is fixed rather than growing during the run.

families_removed.oi_shock_to_rtoken: REMOVED. Bitget exposes only a current open-interest snapshot; every historical OI endpoint returns 404 (40404 Request URL NOT FOUND). A signal defined as OI change over a lookback cannot be backtested. See docs/DATA_FINDINGS.md section 1.

kill_reason_precedence_note: When more than one check fails, the reported reason is the FIRST failing check in this order. The order is preregistered so verdicts are reproducible: it runs from 'the test was not meaningful' (too few observations to compute anything) outward to 'the test was meaningful and the result did not clear the bar'. Checks are all still evaluated and recorded in the entry's `checks` block, so a reader can see every check that failed, not only the one named as the reason.

research_protocol.stage_1_research: The complete preregistered v1.1 enumeration (320 hypotheses) is swept on DISCOVERY, on the frozen store, and adjudicated family-wide at m = 320. A hypothesis survives stage 1 only if it clears every preregistered check.
research_protocol.stage_2_out_of_sample: VALIDATION is read ONLY for hypotheses that passed stage 1, adjudicated at m = the number of stage-1 survivors. If stage 1 promotes nothing, VALIDATION IS NOT READ AT ALL and remains unspent. VALIDATION has never been read by any recorded result in this project: every one of the 201 entries in the v1.0 record used DISCOVERY.
research_protocol.locked_test: NOT READ. LOCKED_TEST was spent by the v1.0 out-of-sample pass on 2026-09-25 (logs/locked-test.jsonl) and is not reusable. v1.1 makes no out-of-sample claim from it and does not touch it.
research_protocol.why_this_shape: A sweep whose family is fixed in advance cannot be re-adjudicated later, so unlike v1.0's live loop there is no promote-then-demote dynamic here. That difference is a CONSEQUENCE of sweeping exhaustively rather than a convenience, and it is recorded because v1.0's headline finding was exactly such a demotion.
